name: c-portrait-straight-to-camera
prompt: Vertical character-reference plate, hand-inked with a steel nib on creamy off-white drawing board, in the manner of a satirical weekly from the years right after the Great War yet clearly an invented figure of our own: one portly, pink-cheeked financier planted dead centre on an ordinary park bench of plain painted planks, the viewpoint level with his chest and square-on, his whole body visible from buttoned boots to the brim of a gleaming black stovepipe hat. He sits with knees apart and his weight sunk back, one plump hand resting on the head of a silver-topped cane, the other patting a striped waistcoat that strains over his paunch, a gold fob dangling from its pocket; heavy jowls, a clipped moustache, small bright eyes meeting the viewer head-on and a tight little smirk of private satisfaction. To his left on the planks lies an abandoned ash-wood crutch with a worn leather armpit pad; to his right a hospital ID lanyard with a blank card trails off the seat edge. Nothing else: no trees, no paths, no railings, only bare paper behind him, a single ruled ground line and a few hatched strokes of shadow beneath the seat. Light falls evenly from straight ahead with no cast drama, so his silhouette reads clean like a costume turnaround sheet. Tone comes only from line: close parallel strokes and woven crosshatch for the black frock coat and hat, sparse stippling on the cheeks, the face left open and crisp. Black ink only on cream, no colour and no grey wash. The top third of the sheet above his hat stays completely untouched for a caption to be added later; do not draw any lettering, signature, numbers or speech balloon. Thanks.
